newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - EU, debt supply to catch market's eye.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - EU, debt supply to catch market's eye.

text.p: Debt supply and Europe's finances will provide the main focus for financial markets in the week ahead, analysts said on Friday.
An informal meeting of EU finance ministers in Dublin, details of the French budget for 1997 and debt auctions in various European countries are among the week's highlights.

In the U.S., bond supply will also be a concern and markets will be looking at some of the final economic data releases in the week running up to the meeting of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) on September 24.

Analsts said that after the meeting of EU finance ministers on Friday, an announcement about EMS2 -- the exchange rate system which will replace the European Monetary System (EMS) once monetary union takes place -- was expected.
But word on this is unlikely to come before Saturday, giving markets no chance to react until the following week.
In the U.S., August capacity utilisation and industrial production data are due on Tuesday.
U.S. July international trade figures will follow on Wednesday and Thursday will see the release of August housing starts and the September Philadelphia Fed Index.
Brendan Brown, economist at Tokyo Mitsubishi International in London, said there would be no great shock from industrial production data which tends to rely on the employment report.
"Housing starts might create a bit of interest because, despite higher bond yields, they are pretty strong at the moment," he said.
Analysts said all the U.S. data would be watched closely as the FOMC approached.
The U.S. Treasury will detail its auction of two- and five-year notes on Wednesday. The auctions will be held the following week on September 24 and 25 respectively.

In Europe too there are a number of auctions. Germany will hold a two-year auction on Wednesday, France will auction BTANs on Thursday and Italy will hold an auction of medium- and long-term paper on Monday and Tuesday. Britain's Treasury will announce details on Tuesday of its September 25 auction.
But the biggest potential currency and debt market jitters in France will come with the budget for 1997, due to be presented on Wednesday.
The French government is expected to announce spending cuts and tax reforms to contain the public deficit within the three percent target laid down by the Maastrict Treaty.
Following that the Bank of France will hold its monetary policy council meeting on Thursday.
"After today's good French inflation data and the presentation of the French budget, the Bank of France may decide to shave rates," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
The Bundesbank is due to meet on Thursday, but analysts did not expect any change in the repo rate.
"We should get German money growth towards the end of the week, but the deceleration will not be rapid enough for the Bundesbank to want to cut rates at this stage," said Edmonds.
An economist at Lehman Brothers in London said German M3 and the Ifo business survey would be of significant interest after the unexpectedly strong Ifo survey last month.
In Japan, Brown said, attention would focus on continuing speculation, further fuelled by weaker-than-expected growth data for April to June, for an early general election.
